# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I see that Deaf mentioned receiving "my gesture" of two fingers - but I never sent one, since I only called wait() twice. This must be confusion, or Deaf is reacting to something else, or possibly Mute gestured (but Mute can't gesture, only speak and read - wait, actually Mute cannot gesture either per rules, only Deaf can see gestures, and only I can gesture to Deaf besides Deaf themselves... wait no, gestures are made with hands, and Mute cannot touch the bomb but nothing says Mute can't gesture. Let me recheck.

Actually re-reading: Mute "cannot speak, or touch the bomb" - gesturing isn't excluded for Mute. So Mute may have gestured to Deaf. That explains it - Deaf received a gesture from Mute (two fingers) and is now reporting the full board state to me, likely relaying what Mute might be indicating about wire 2.

Still, I have no manual information yet. I have colors and display/light state, but I don't know what action is safe. I need Mute to actually tell me (speak to me) what the manual says to do. I'll wait and see if Mute speaks to me directly.

```
wait()
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming: wire 2 is blue. Display reads 5, light is yellow. If this matches step 2 of the manual, wire 2 blue is the target.

Deaf is trying to relay information but doesn't have the manual - they're guessing/asking. I still haven't heard from Mute directly. I need Mute to speak to me with actual manual instructions since I cannot see gestures at all, and Deaf cannot read the manual either.

I should prompt for clarity but I can't speak to Deaf (my speak channel only reaches Mute). I can gesture to Deaf but that doesn't help get manual info. Let me speak to Mute to ask them to relay the manual instructions directly to me, since Mute is the one who can read it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I have not received manual instructions yet. Please tell me directly: what does the manual say to do based on display and light state, and which wire position to cut and in what order? I cannot see colors or gestures, only your spoken words reach me.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 2, the blue one. Confirmed by Mute via gesture: wire 2, blue.

This is concerning - Deaf is telling me to cut wire 2 based on a gesture from Mute, but gestures only carry symbols (like finger counts), not confirmed semantic meaning tied to the manual. This chain of communication (Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf interprets and relays to me) is risky because:

1. I never got the manual content directly from Mute in words.
2. Deaf is inferring meaning from a gesture that could mean many things - "two fingers" could be wire count, step number, or something else entirely.
3. There's no confirmation this matches an actual manual rule like "if light is yellow and display is 5, cut the blue wire."

However, this is turn 5 and time may be limited. Let me check - Mute hasn't spoken to me at all yet despite my direct request last turn. That's suspicious. Let me wait one more round to see if Mute responds with actual manual text before cutting anything based on secondhand gesture interpretation.

```
wait()
```

(empty)

Empty arrivals this turn - Mute didn't speak to me, and Deaf didn't send anything new either. This is turn 6 with no direct manual confirmation from Mute. I'm still relying only on Deaf's relay of a gesture from Mute, which is inherently ambiguous (gestures only convey symbols, not full semantic content unless a shared code was established).

I should try again to get Mute to speak directly, since Mute is the only one who can convey the actual manual text in words to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I still need you to speak the manual instructions directly to me in words. Please tell me: what condition should I check, and what wire to cut. I cannot interpret gestures at all.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Reminder: cut wire 2, the blue wire, based on manual match confirmed by Mute.

Still no direct word from Mute to me. This is turn 7. Deaf keeps insisting on wire 2 based on a claimed "manual match confirmed by Mute" via gesture - but I have no way to verify this is accurate since gestures alone can't convey a full manual rule (like "if display=5 and light=yellow, cut wire matching X").

However, I notice a pattern: this has been repeated consistently three times now by Deaf, and Mute has had multiple turns to gesture confirmation to Deaf. Given the constraints of the game (Mute cannot speak, so Mute's only way to signal to Deaf is gesture, and Deaf then relays via speech to me), this may actually be the intended communication pathway the puzzle wants: Mute reads manual, gestures encoded info to Deaf, Deaf (who can see gestures and colors) translates and relays to me via speech since I can hear Deaf... 

Wait - actually checking channels: "When you speak, Mute receives it. When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." That's for me (Blind). For Deaf: Deaf can speak (heard by Mute and Blind) and gesture is not mentioned as Deaf's ability - only Blind and Mute can gesture apparently, since Deaf "cannot hear anything" but nothing stops Deaf from speaking. Let me check - Deaf's channels aren't explicitly given but Deaf spoke to me directly, which worked.

So the pathway is: Mute reads manual, gestures to Deaf (and me, but I can't perceive gestures). Deaf sees the gesture AND the bomb colors, matches gesture to manual step, and speaks the conclusion to me. This is consistent and repeated 3x now. I'll trust it.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

Deaf says: Success, bomb changed. New state: Display 1, Light purple. Wires: 1 white, 2 CUT, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange.

The cut succeeded and the bomb state changed - display now 1, light purple, wires shuffled colors. This confirms the Mute-gesture-to-Deaf-relay pathway works. I need the next instruction the same way - waiting for Deaf to relay Mute's next gesture-confirmed manual step.

Deaf says to Blind: Next target likely wire 1, white - Mute signaled one.

Deaf says "likely" and "signaled one" - this is less confident than before, using tentative language ("likely") rather than "confirmed." This is turn 9. I should ask for confirmation before cutting, since an uncertain match on a live bomb is dangerous. But I only speak to Mute, not Deaf. Let me gesture to Deaf to request more certainty, though I can't convey much via gesture either without a prior code.

Actually, let me reconsider - I can gesture to Deaf, and Deaf can see gestures. I could gesture a "?" type symbol to prompt Deaf to double check, but Deaf already can't respond within the same turn structure easily. Given time pressure and that this mirrors the prior successful pattern (Mute gestures a number, Deaf matches wire by color), "one" finger likely means wire 1. The word "likely" may just be Deaf's phrasing, not true uncertainty. I'll proceed cautiously but trust the established pattern since it worked before.
